PUO.title: Fever of unknown origin (PUO)

items: Fever of unknown origin is a fever where the cause is not found after the first checks.
Doctors usually define it as a temperature of 38.3 degrees C or more on several occasions.
Ongoing fever, with or without other signs such as weight loss or tiredness.
A repeat, detailed history and examination.
Blood tests including blood count, inflammation markers, liver and kidney tests, and urine tests.
Several sets of blood cultures, and a chest X-ray and abdominal ultrasound.
CT scan if the first tests do not help, and an echocardiogram if there is a heart murmur or a risk.
Treatment depends on the cause that is found. Your team will explain the plan.

sections.h: What you can do at home
items: Keep a daily record of your temperature and symptoms to share with your team.
Your team will repeat tests and review your progress.
This leaflet gives general information. Follow your doctor's advice.

urgent: Fever with low blood pressure, confusion, or breathlessness
Fever with a new heart murmur or a rash
